## Review of PR #4028 at `3764e7ed9` - Needs changes before merge

This is a SAFETY-tier review. The PR changes toolpaths and posted G-code (2D Adaptive entry, piece order and the end of each level).

The code and the tests are good. I found no gouge, crash or wrong-output defect. One process item blocks the merge: the body has no before/after screenshots of the changed UI.

### What looks good

- The start point is the seed of the HSM plan. It goes through the same `triangle_about` / `dive_room` entry law as the automatic seed. A pick that has no room is refused by name. The pick is never moved.
- The exit run-back uses the posted moves in reverse. A reversed line is the same line. A reversed arc keeps its `center` and flips `ccw` (`ArcMove` has only `center`, `ccw`, `plane`), so it is the same arc. The run-back cuts no new material.
- `reseat_climb` moves only the level climb and the `from` point of the next rapid. I probed the level links (see "Probe"): the level climb goes to the clearance height, so the moved rapid is at a safe height.
- A plan that falls back to the Offset rings or the trochoid is refused when a pick is set (`fallback_refusal`). A picked start that keeps an overload note is refused (`overload_refusal`).
- Without a pick, no new code changes the path. `golden_cl` and the three example catalog suites are green, with no golden moved.
- No `unwrap`, `expect` or `panic!` in new non-test code. Index access in `run_back` is bounded (`rposition`, `get`).
- The new code is in the correct crates. `adaptive_pick_op.rs` in `app` reads `OpParams` (the document). The planner logic is in `motion`. The new tests join existing directory suites. The decision file is present.
- The WCS yaw turns the picks into the generation frame. A test pins it at 90 degrees.

### Results (trial merge with `upstream/main` `3bb6647f6`, local Mac, sccache)

The trial merge is clean. GitHub says `MERGEABLE`.

- `motion` quick steps: 99 steps, 0 failed (build, `lib` and all 97 mapped suites, including `pass_start_levels`, `adaptive_hsm`, `adaptive_entry_pieces`, `avoid_adaptive`, `optimal_load`, `shape_masks`, `level_links`).
- `app` suites: `start_exit_shared`, `golden_cl`, `example_catalog`, `example_catalog_adaptive`, `example_catalog_edge_work`, `adaptive_pass_start`, `do_not_touch_adaptive`, `pick_doors`, `adaptive_trochoid`, `adaptive_pinch`, `adaptive_zero_margin_island`, `adaptive_fig8_crossing`, `pocket_pass_start`, `rest_adaptive_op`, `shoulder_adaptive`, `slot_start_exit`, `slot_picks`, `area_picks`, `opframe_picks`, `mcp_pockets`, `solid_law_goldens`: 21 steps, 0 failed.
- Extra suites run (they read the changed `tests/golden/` directory): `contour_arc_fit_wall`, `hole_wall_flats`, `hole_wall_pins`, `wall_arc_entry`, `wall_column_gouge`: all ok.
- `ui suites: lib` and `ui suites: operations`: ok.
- `cargo xtask gate light`: 6 steps, 0 failed.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-motion -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-ui --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.
- I did not run the other 680 mapped `app` suites. They do not read the changed code paths, and the author's full quick gate on this head reports 875 steps, 0 failed.
- Heavy lanes: not run. This is a `P2` PR, so no heavy step is required (AGENTS.md "Heavy lanes at review").
- No importer or `testdata/` change, so no kernel STEP suites are required.

### Mutations (both red as expected; reverted)

1. `exit_on_path` returns the path unchanged when an exit point is set. Red: `pass_start_levels` (`the_exit_point_is_where_the_last_pass_ends_on_each_level`, `a_point_the_plan_cannot_hold_is_refused_by_name`) and `start_exit_shared` (`the_entry_is_at_..._exit_point` with its golden, `the_picks_hold_under_a_90_degree_wcs_yaw`, `a_point_..._nothing_is_cut`).
2. `choose_entry` ignores the start point, and `overload_refusal` always returns `None`. Red: `pass_start_levels` (`the_start_point_is_where_the_helix_goes_down_on_each_level`, `a_point_..._refused_by_name`) and `start_exit_shared` (4 tests, including the undo/file/stamp test).

### Probe (local scratch test, reverted)

I cut the 60 x 40 rectangle and an L-shaped area (60 x 40 without its 30 x 20 top-right quarter) with exit points on different walls. I used `retract_z` 1.0 and `None`. In each case the level climb went to the clearance height (5.0), and the moved rapid started there. The in-level links at the retract height were not changed. The L cut with exit (59, 10) ended each level at (54.983, 10.000).

### Goldens

No golden moved. The new golden `adaptive2d_start_exit_picks.cl` is in the reach of the tool centre (X and Y within -11 .. 11). Z is between 15 and 25. The helix is about (-4, -3) with radius 1. The last feed ends at (11, 0), the wall point nearest the exit point (14, 0). The last move climbs to clearance.

### Requested before merge

1. **No before/after screenshots** (blocking). The PR adds the Start point and Exit point groups to the 2D Adaptive Lead in / Lead out tab (`crates/ui/src/egui_app/op_page.rs:156`, `crates/ui/src/egui_app/start_exit_rows.rs:92-112`), and the viewport pick and marks for the 2D Adaptive. Add a before and an after screenshot of that tab to the PR body. Put the images on the fork's `pr-screenshots` branch and link them. Do not commit images to the PR branch.
2. **The exit help text does not agree with the behaviour** (small, fix in the same round). `crates/ui/src/egui_app/start_exit_rows.rs:102` says "the last pass of each level runs on along its closing lap". The code runs back along the closing ride, in reverse (`exit_on_path`; the decision file item 3 says so, and it drops "running on" because no closed lap exists). Change the text to say that the tool runs back along its last pass to the point nearest the exit point.

### Notes (not blocking)

- The "Do not touch" keep-out refusal, the "climb out" refusal and the "exit at the start's piece" refusal have no pinning fixture. The body says so. Follow-up suggestion: `P7`, one test for each refusal.
- `crates/motion/src/approach.rs` grows from 467 to 479 lines. It was already over 400 lines.
- `exit_on_path` runs on each call of `pocket_over_with_relief`. If one operation calls it more than one time (for example, for separate areas), each part path runs back to the same exit point or is refused. This agrees with "refused, never moved", but no test covers it.
- `run_back` looks only at the start point of an arc, not at points inside the arc. The nearest point can thus be a little farther than the true nearest point. This is safe: the reach check uses that distance.

The author is a collaborator and not the reviewing account, so I do not change the ready state of the PR.

The author's agent stopped work on this PR when the maintainer took it over. Nothing was pushed to this PR branch. The unpushed review-fix work is on a side branch for reuse:

https://github.com/qsmits/Camcraft/compare/issue/3327-adaptive-picks...handoff/4028-review-fixes

- `d3c790aca`: the exit help text in `start_exit_rows.rs` now says that the tool runs back along its last pass to the point nearest the exit point (review item 2).
- `979e2801c`: a layout fix and two tests.
  - The Clear button row in the shared Start point / Exit point group is now one row high. Before, it took the free height and pushed the safety line out of view (2D Contour, Slot and 2D Adaptive).
  - New pins: `a_start_or_exit_point_in_the_keepout_is_refused_by_name` (`avoid_adaptive`) and `an_exit_at_the_start_piece_is_refused_by_name` (`pass_start_levels`).
- `162114a90`, `fb5cb618e`: merges of main. The conflict in `pick_kinds.rs` keeps both arms. A duplicate `mod common;` line in `start_exit_shared.rs` is removed.
- Screenshots (review item 1): https://github.com/qsmits/Camcraft/tree/pr-screenshots/pr-4028 (before from main `267ee5096`, after from the branch).

Not done: no green gate on the final head `fb5cb618e` (the last run was stopped on purpose). The light lane and strict clippy did not run. The climb-out refusal has no pin: a KeepDown level link still lifts to the retract plane, so the refusal does not fire.

@qsmits @NeoTech: we can help finish this one. The plan: start from qsmits's `handoff/4028-review-fixes` branch, close the open findings of the review of `3764e7ed9`, merge main (the PR conflicts with it now), gate it, and push to this PR (maintainer edits are allowed). The PR stays qsmits's, and we would only add commits.

The comments say the maintainer took this PR over, so we won't start until one of you says OK here, or tells us that someone else already has it.
Withdrawn: the maintainer has this PR, so we're staying off it. No reply needed.
